newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar seen struggling at 1.60 DM - Handelsblatt.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen struggling at 1.60 DM - Handelsblatt.

text.p: German currency market experts polled by the Handelsblatt financial daily on Monday said the U.S. dollar, although firm, would struggle to extend its rally through 1.60 marks.
The analysts said the mark's weakness stemmed from a slack economy, as well as its planned link to weaker currencies under European monetary union -- which most expected to go ahead on time in 1999.
"The dollar would have to jump clearly above 1.60 marks to open the way higher," Michael Schnirel of BHF Bank told the newspaper. "But I don't think it will make it soon."

The Handelsblatt survey, due for publication on Tuesday, was released after the dollar set a 27-month high at above 1.59 marks based on stronger U.S. growth in late 1996 and Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's support of a strong dollar.
Hans-Joerg Naumer, at Societe Generale in Frankfurt, said economic fundamentals in the United States and Germany were running in opposite directions.

He said he saw the dollar clearing 1.60 marks this week, while the nearing of monetary union later in the year -- and the resulting loss in importance of the mark -- would weaken the German currency further.
West-LB analyst Frank Richter said recent dramatic gains by sterling against the mark had been overdone and could be corrected in the summer.
He added that, if high budget deficits in the second half of the year point to a delay in a wider monetary union, the mark could appreciate against other European currencies.

Other analysts said that more important for exchange rates than EMU was the possibility that German interest rates could fall, while the next move in the U.S. is likely to be upwards -- moves which are likely to favour the dollar against the mark.
